title: Calcutta High Court Upholds Injunction Against 'IJM Gold Stag' Cigarettes Over ITC's 'Gold Flake' Marks
case_name: Pravin Kumar v. ITC Limited & Ors.
card_summary: A Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court dismissed an appeal against an injunction restraining 'IJM Gold Stag' cigarettes, finding a prima facie case of infringement and passing off against ITC's 'Gold Flake' marks. It held 'Gold' has acquired secondary meaning through ITC's long use, and that the 85 per cent of a pack taken up by health warnings cannot be ignored when comparing packs.
card_tip: On a cramped pack where most of the surface is a mandatory health warning, courts still compare the remaining branding closely; a crowded label is no shield against a passing off claim.
verification_notes: Confirmed across LiveLaw, Verdictum and King Stubb & Kasiva; all three agree on the Division Bench's findings on secondary meaning and the health-warning point. Sources differ on whether the Single Judge's original 2025 order rested on passing off alone or also on infringement, so the card states only the Division Bench's own confirmed finding.
